title: 2014 Ram 1500 / Grand Cherokee 3.0 EcoDiesel: "rumble strip" shudder at cruise, both cylinder heads
summary: FCA bulletin 09-004-17: a brief shudder at 50-70 mph and 1,600-2,000 rpm on the 3.0L diesel, no DTCs, often felt on the 6-7 upshift. Carbon from light-load driving; the fix is both cylinder heads with revised valve stem seals plus a PCM update.

steps.text: Customer describes a slight shudder that feels and sounds like driving over rumble strips; it can be mistaken for a transmission problem or a misfire.

Conditions to reproduce it: steady 50-70 mph, 1,600-2,000 rpm, warming up after a cold soak, a few seconds at a time and often on the 6-7 upshift, light acceleration or a slight grade. It goes away with hard throttle or a closed-throttle decel.
Check all engine systems with the scan tool first. Repair any other DTCs or symptoms before going further with this bulletin.
If the test drive or the customer's description matches, replace both cylinder heads (new heads have valve stem seals designed to stop the carbon build-up from light-load driving).
Make sure the PCM has the latest software afterwards.

body: If the shudder can't be reproduced and the description doesn't match the listed conditions, the bulletin says it does not apply and further diagnosis is needed.

sources.title: Service Bulletin 09-004-17: Intermittent Engine Shudder While Driving
